title: Algebraically trivial lines on a smooth affine product come from its factors
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $X,Y$ be smooth geometrically integral affine finite-type $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. For a finite-type $k$-scheme $Z$, let $\operatorname{Pic}(Z)$ mean the group of isomorphism classes of invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module], with tensor product as addition. Define $\operatorname{Pic}^{\mathrm{alg}}(Z)$ to be the subgroup generated by the differences $[L_{s_1}]-[L_{s_0}]$, where $S$ is a smooth connected separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $s_0,s_1\in S(k)$, and $L$ is an invertible module on $Z\times_k S$; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion and connected means its point space is not a union of two disjoint nonempty open subsets. Products and tensor pullbacks are [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback]. If $p_X,p_Y$ are the two projections, then
$$\operatorname{Pic}^{\mathrm{alg}}(X\times_kY)=p_X^*\operatorname{Pic}^{\mathrm{alg}}(X)+p_Y^*\operatorname{Pic}^{\mathrm{alg}}(Y).$$
In particular, every invertible module $N$ whose class belongs to the left side admits invertible modules $A$ on $X$ and $B$ on $Y$, with classes in the respective subgroups, and an isomorphism $N\cong p_X^*A\otimes p_Y^*B$.

proof.text: Put $T=X\times_kY$. Smooth base change and composition make $T$ smooth; the geometric irreducibility product theorem and geometric reducedness of smooth schemes make it geometrically integral, hence connected and nonempty. It is affine (the spectrum of the tensor product of the two affine coordinate algebras), hence separated over $k$ because a morphism with affine source is separated; the same applies to $X$ and $Y$. It is of finite type by finite-type base change and composition. Choose $x_0\in X(k)$ and $y_0\in Y(k)$ using density of rational points on nonempty smooth schemes. For the difficult inclusion it suffices to treat each defining generator $[L_{s_1}]-[L_{s_0}]$ of $\operatorname{Pic}^{\mathrm{alg}}(T)$: sums and negatives of external classes are external classes, using tensor products and duals on the factors.

proof.text: Apply projective-curve interpolation with $Z=T$ to this generator. It gives a smooth projective geometrically integral curve $C$, points $a,b\in C(k)$, and an invertible module $E$ on $T\times_k C$ with $E_a\cong L_{s_0}$ and $E_b\cong L_{s_1}$. Thus the generator is $[E_b]-[E_a]$. The hypotheses on $T$ needed by interpolation were established in step 1; the original parameter $S$ has exactly the smoothness, connectedness, separatedness and finite-type hypotheses in that lemma.

source.place: Chapter I Theorem 3.4 (product-axis rigidity), Theorem 5.16 and Corollary 5.18 (see-saw), combined with the curve Jacobian and projective parameter interpolation; agent-assembled Picard argument for Guo Claim 5.2.1.

proof.text:
Write $E_X=E|_{X\times\{y_0\}\times C}$, $E_Y=E|_{\{x_0\}\times Y\times C}$ and $E_0=E|_{\{(x_0,y_0)\}\times C}$. With $r_X:T\times C\to X\times C$, $r_Y:T\times C\to Y\times C$ and $r_C:T\times C\to C$, form
$$H=E\otimes r_X^*E_X^{-1}\otimes r_Y^*E_Y^{-1}\otimes r_C^*E_0.$$
On the $X$-axis the first two factors cancel, and the last two are the inverse pullback of $E_0$ and its pullback; on the $Y$-axis the same cancellation holds with $X,Y$ interchanged. Hence both axis restrictions are trivial on the entire product with $C$. These identities use functoriality and tensor compatibility of pullback; inverse means the dual invertible module.

source.place: Chapter I Theorem 3.4 (product-axis rigidity), Theorem 5.16 and Corollary 5.18 (see-saw), combined with the curve Jacobian and projective parameter interpolation; agent-assembled Picard argument for Guo Claim 5.2.1.

proof.text: Regard $H$ as a family of lines on $C$ parameterized by $T$. Its fibrewise degree is locally constant on the connected scheme $T$, and is zero at $(x_0,y_0)$ because that fibre is trivial. Thus its Picard class lies in the degree-zero Picard functor on $T$. The Jacobian representability theorem identifies this group-valued functor with $h_{J_C}$, so this class determines a morphism $\alpha:T\to J_C$. Naturality identifies its restrictions to the two axes with the classes of the trivial families from step 3; therefore both restrictions are the identity morphism. Apply product-axis rigidity to the smooth geometrically integral factors $X,Y$, their chosen rational points, and the abelian variety $J_C$. It yields $\alpha=0$. In particular, for every $t\in T(k)$ the actual line $H_t$ on $C$ is trivial: the Jacobian theorem identifies $J_C(k)$ with degree-zero line-module isomorphism classes, not merely numerical classes.

source.place: Chapter I Theorem 3.4 (product-axis rigidity), Theorem 5.16 and Corollary 5.18 (see-saw), combined with the curve Jacobian and projective parameter interpolation; agent-assembled Picard argument for Guo Claim 5.2.1.

proof.text:
Use see-saw with proper geometrically integral factor $C$, point $a$, smooth separated finite-type parameter $T$, and the family $H$ whose every rational fibre was shown trivial in step 4. It gives $H\cong\operatorname{pr}_T^*(H_a)$. Restricting to $b$ and $a$ gives $[H_b]-[H_a]=0$ in $\operatorname{Pic}(T)$. Expanding the definition of $H$ therefore gives
$$[E_b]-[E_a]=p_X^*([ (E_X)_b]-[(E_X)_a])+p_Y^*([(E_Y)_b]-[(E_Y)_a]).$$
The remaining term from $E_0$ disappears because each of its fibres at $a,b$ is a one-dimensional $k$-vector space, hence gives a trivial line on $T$. The two differences on the right belong to the respective algebraically trivial subgroups: $C$ itself is an allowed smooth connected separated finite-type parameter. This proves the inclusion for each generator and hence for their subgroup.

source.place: Chapter I Theorem 3.4 (product-axis rigidity), Theorem 5.16 and Corollary 5.18 (see-saw), combined with the curve Jacobian and projective parameter interpolation; agent-assembled Picard argument for Guo Claim 5.2.1.

proof.text: For the reverse inclusion, pull back any defining family on $X\times S$ along $p_X\times\mathrm{id}_S$. Its two fibres are the pullbacks of the original fibres, so every generator from $X$ pulls back to a generator on $T$; the same argument applies to $Y$. Thus the sum of the two pullback subgroups lies in $\operatorname{Pic}^{\mathrm{alg}}(T)$. Equality follows. Finally, write any class in the right side as $p_X^*[A]+p_Y^*[B]$, with $[A]$ and $[B]$ in the stated subgroups. The definition of $\operatorname{Pic}$ as line-module isomorphism classes turns this class equality into $N\cong p_X^*A\otimes p_Y^*B$.
